newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN STAINLESS STEEL TRADE SEES HIGHER SALES.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN STAINLESS STEEL TRADE SEES HIGHER SALES.

text.p: Germany's stainless steel trade association EHV said higher volume sales in 1997 should not be accompanied by much improved profits.

"Our members are more than content with volumes, there has not been a summer lull and there is still an order backlog," said an official at the association, which represents stockholders and processors.
"Steel consumers are busy due an upswing in export demand which has been supported by the low mark...but the price of stainless steel is now falling and this will weigh on profits."
The association forecast German stainless steel output at 1.40 million tonnes this year compared with 1.28 million in 1996.
Stainless steel accounts for two thirds of nickel use.
The association said nickel use in German stainless steel could be 56,500 tonnes in 1997 after 51,000 tonnes last year.

Service centres organised in EHV raised their Jan-June sales of stainless sheet by five percent while long products sales rose by between 10 and 15 percent and tube sales were up by between nine percent (seamless) and 20 percent (welded).
Nickel surcharges which had risen earlier this year during earlier nickel rallies were stable in August.
The surcharge in 18-10 percent chrome-nickel steel was 560 marks a tonne in May, 570 in June, 560 in July, 550 in August and would be unchanged from August in September, EHV said.
Its members's supplies were now at around 75 days of use compared with a desirable 60 days target, it also said.
But high levels of demand in August should help reduce stocks and prevent massive price pressure.
